Merge and rebase both bring one branch's changes into another, but they leave different footprints.

**Merge** adds a new commit that ties two branches together. Your history keeps every twist and turn, but on a busy branch it can get messy.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of the other branch, one by one. History ends up a clean straight line, but it rewrites the commits, so their identity changes.

The rule that matters most: never rebase commits other people have already pulled. It rewrites history, so it can wreck their copy of the branch.

- Working alone on a feature branch and want tidy history: rebase.
- Bringing changes into a shared branch like `main`: merge.
- Branch already pushed and others are using it: merge, not rebase.
